threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, objectives, and roles before detailed planning starts.

messages.text: Kicking off the Integrated Youth Wellbeing and Outreach Pilot Programme channel. I have shared the Pilot Programme Overview and Objectives from project_pack_ref: Integrated Youth Wellbeing and Outreach Pilot Programme (see A1). The aim is a 3‑month pilot improving psychosocial support, health literacy, and inclusion for at‑risk youth. In this thread, we need to: 1) confirm which youth groups and locations we will focus on, and 2) be clear who is leading outreach, workshops, and oral health sessions. Please read A1 and then share your view on priority youth groups and locations, referencing any early thinking from T1, T5, and T6.

Thanks for sharing A1. For T1, my first thought on target youth groups: 1) young people already known to social services for family stress or housing issues, 2) those flagged by schools for attendance or behaviour concerns, and 3) youth hanging around the community centre after school with no structured activities. Locations could be the main secondary school, the community centre, and the youth drop‑in room at the clinic. I have not validated these yet with the social services manager, so this is a draft list.

From a logistics angle for T6, plotting locations on the map for A6 later: the secondary school, community centre, and clinic are all within a 20‑minute radius. If we add the smaller satellite school on the east side, travel time jumps and we may struggle to keep within existing staff hours. I suggest we initially focus on: 1) main secondary school, 2) community centre, 3) clinic youth room. We can add the satellite school only if we see capacity later.

On T5 and A5, for the oral health part I can run awareness and basic screening at the clinic youth room and possibly at the community centre if we can bring portable mirrors and disposable kits. Doing screenings at the school might be harder without a proper space and consent process. I would prefer we start with clinic and community centre for oral health sessions, then review if school‑based activities are realistic.

From the documentation side, once T1 and T6 are clearer I can help format a simple one‑pager listing target youth groups and locations so everyone is aligned. That will also feed into T4 and T7 later. For now, I am hearing three main groups: 1) youth already in contact with social services, 2) those flagged by schools, 3) informal groups at the community centre and clinic. Can we confirm if we are including any youth from the satellite school at this stage or not?

Good summary. Before we lock anything, I want to check two things: 1) safeguarding coverage at each site, and 2) staff availability within normal working hours, as A1 stresses. @1424, can you check with the social services manager whether we have safeguarding focal points at the community centre and clinic youth room for the pilot period? That will influence whether we can include all three locations from the start.

I can check that. I will speak with the social services manager this afternoon about safeguarding coverage and get confirmation on which locations are approved. I will also ask whether the satellite school is realistic for this pilot or better left for a later phase. I will report back here so we can finalise T1.

Once we have that confirmation, I will draft the first version of the field visit schedule and routing for T6. My working assumption is: 2 afternoons per week at the main secondary school, 1 afternoon at the community centre, and 1 slot at the clinic youth room. I will build in buffer time for travel and possible timetable changes, as the risks section in A1 highlights.

To be clear on roles for oral health: I can lead the practical side of T5 sessions (set up, basic screening, health education messages aligned with A5), but I will need the dental clinic supervisor to validate the protocol and messages before we use them. I can also support youth engagement by making the sessions interactive, but I will rely on @1424 and @89329 to connect with young people they already know.

On roles more broadly, based on T3, T4, and T7: @89329 leads the wellbeing workshop curriculum and facilitation; @1424 leads outreach and case follow‑up; I will handle templates and youth‑facing materials; @98920 leads oral health sessions; and @522004 leads scheduling and data tables. Does that match how you see it, or is anything missing for D2?

That role split sounds right to me. I am happy to take lead on the workshop curriculum (T3) and overall group facilitation, and to coordinate with school leadership and the community health coordinator when needed. For D2, I would like @1424 and @98920 to confirm they are comfortable with the outreach and oral health leads as described, and @522004 to confirm the logistics and data support role.

I am fine to own T6 and later T12. I will also keep an eye on attendance patterns so we can adjust the schedule if engagement is low in certain slots. I will not make changes directly with schools without checking with you first, but I can prepare options.

I am comfortable leading the oral health sessions under T5 and T11. I will coordinate with the dental clinic supervisor to make sure A5 and the checklist in A7 are followed. I will need help with scheduling those sessions into the wider programme so they do not clash with key school activities.

I can take the lead on outreach and follow‑up, including T1 and T8, and on monitoring weekly participation for T10. I will need some guidance from you on how best to structure the group sessions at the start, but I can handle contact with youth and families and keep records as we go.

Update after speaking with the social services manager: we have approval to focus on three locations for the pilot: 1) main secondary school, 2) community centre, 3) clinic youth room. The satellite school is not included for now due to staffing limits. These three sites already have safeguarding arrangements in place, which will be detailed further in T2 and A2.

Thanks for confirming. Based on this, I propose we record D1 as: target youth groups are 1) youth already known to social services for family or housing stress, 2) students flagged by the main secondary school for attendance or behaviour concerns, and 3) informal groups using the community centre and clinic youth room. Locations are the main secondary school, community centre, and clinic youth room only. Unless anyone objects today, we will treat this as final for the pilot.

On D2, summarising what we have agreed: outreach and case follow‑up lead: 1424 (T1, T8, T10); wellbeing workshops lead: 89329 (T3, T9); documentation and materials: 61769 (T4, T7); oral health sessions and materials: 98920 (T5, T11); field schedule and data tables: 522004 (T6, T12). I will share this with the social services manager for awareness, but within the team we can treat this as our working agreement.

I will draft a short roles and responsibilities note summarising D1 and D2 and store it with A1 so everyone can find it easily. I will also prepare a simple visual of the three locations and main activities for each, which we can use when briefing school leadership and the community health coordinator.

threads.thread_goal: Define safeguarding, confidentiality, and record-keeping standards.

messages.text: I have uploaded a first draft of the safeguarding and confidentiality procedures for the pilot, based on A2 and aligned with T2. The draft covers one‑to‑one and group settings, consent, information sharing, and how we handle disclosures. In this thread, please review and comment, especially on what minimum data we should record for each youth interaction so we can align T4, T8, and A3.

I have read through the draft A2. It is clear on not promising absolute confidentiality and on when we must share information for safety. For record‑keeping in T8, I think we should at least record: first name or code, date, location, brief reason for contact, and any follow‑up agreed. I am not sure how detailed the notes should be for group sessions versus one‑to‑one, so I would appreciate guidance.

For T4 and A3, I suggest we separate: 1) attendance and basic participation data, and 2) more sensitive case notes. For attendance, we can use anonymised IDs plus age band and school or community site. For case notes under T8, we can keep more detail but restrict access. That way, the templates in A3 stay simple enough for staff with basic computer skills, as required in the project constraints.

From a data perspective and thinking ahead to T12, we need enough fields to see patterns but not so many that forms are left incomplete. I propose the minimum data fields for each interaction (for D4) are: anonymised ID, age band, gender (optional), location, type of contact (workshop, one‑to‑one, oral health session), and a short coded reason for contact. Free‑text notes can be kept separately in T8 for those who need them.

For oral health sessions under T5 and T11, I want to be sure we are not recording any clinical details that go beyond the pilot scope. Would it be enough if we record: anonymised ID, whether the youth attended the oral health session, and a simple flag like needs dental follow‑up yes or no, which we then pass to the dental clinic supervisor through the usual clinical system?

Yes, for oral health we should keep it simple and avoid storing clinical details in the pilot records. The clinical notes stay in the dental system. For the pilot, we only need to know that a youth attended, received education, and whether a referral was made. We will also make sure the consent section in A2 is clear about this separation.

I can design the attendance and feedback templates in A3 to include the fields you listed: anonymised ID, age band, location, type of contact, and a short coded reason. For feedback, I will add 3 or 4 simple questions with smiley‑face scales so young people can respond quickly. I will share a draft for T4 later today for comments.

On the anonymised ID, I want to be sure I can still link a young person to their notes if they come back. Would it work if I keep a separate key list with real names and IDs in a locked file, while the shared templates only show the ID? I will need to be careful not to mix them up, so any tips on a simple system would help.

Keeping a separate key list is a good approach, but we should have only one or two people with access to it. I suggest you and the social services manager hold that list, and we do not upload it to shared folders. For the rest of us, we only see anonymised IDs in A3 and in any tables I compile for T12.

I will add a short section in T2 describing exactly that: a separate ID key held securely by a named person, not shared in the general project folder. I will also clarify how long we keep records and how we store paper forms versus digital ones, in line with data privacy rules.

Quick question on consent: for group workshops, do we rely on existing school consent forms, or do we need a separate pilot‑specific consent? It affects how we design the header of the attendance sheet in A3.

For school‑based group workshops, we can rely on existing school consent where it already covers wellbeing activities, but we must confirm this with school leadership. For clinic and community centre sessions, we will use a short pilot‑specific consent form. I will note this in T2 and A2 and check with the data and compliance officer before we finalise.

For oral health consent, I will align with the dental clinic supervisor so that our pilot consent wording matches the clinic standard. I will share any specific phrases we must use so they can be added into A2 and the templates in A3 where relevant.

To close D4, can we agree that the minimum data fields for each youth interaction are: anonymised ID, age band, location, type of contact, and a short coded reason for contact, plus an optional flag for referral made yes or no? More detailed notes will sit in the secure counselling records under T8. If no one objects by tomorrow morning, I will treat this as agreed and update T2 and A3 accordingly.

On D3, I will now incorporate all feedback into the safeguarding and confidentiality document T2, then send it to the social services manager and the data and compliance officer for review. Assuming they are satisfied, we will adopt A2 as the reference for the pilot. I will confirm in this channel once they sign off.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise workshop curriculum and oral health session design.

messages.text: I have shared the first draft of the Youth Wellbeing Workshop Curriculum Pack (A4) and the initial outline of the Oral Health Awareness and Screening Protocol (A5), linked to T3 and T5. In this thread, we need to agree the initial set of wellbeing workshop topics and sequence for D5, and confirm which oral health activities are feasible within our time and resources for D6. Please review A4 and A5 and share comments.

For the wellbeing workshops (T3), I am proposing 8 core sessions: 1) getting to know each other and ground rules, 2) stress and coping, 3) friendships and peer pressure, 4) emotions and mood, 5) online life and safety, 6) health and sleep, 7) planning for the future, 8) celebration and next steps. Each session has simple activities and links to local support services. Feedback welcome, especially on language and cultural fit.

The topics in A4 look relevant to what young people talk about with me. I wonder if we should bring the online life and safety session earlier, maybe as session 3, because many issues start there. Also, could we include a short part on family stress somewhere, maybe in the stress and coping session, since that comes up a lot?

From a materials perspective for T7, the activities in A4 are manageable to type and format into handouts. I suggest we keep each session to one main worksheet plus a simple reflection card, so printing stays low‑cost. I can also adjust wording to be clearer for younger teens if needed.

Thinking ahead to scheduling in A6 and T6, 8 sessions per group fits well into the 3‑month pilot if we run one session per week at each site. We just need to avoid exam weeks at the school. If we move the online life session earlier as suggested, it will not affect logistics, but we should keep the celebration session at the end for closure.

On A5 and T5, I have outlined three components for oral health sessions: 1) short interactive talk on brushing, sugar, and visiting the dentist, 2) basic visual screening with a torch and disposable mirror, 3) signposting and referrals for those who need follow‑up. Given time limits, I think we can realistically do 20 minutes for the talk and 20 minutes for screenings per small group, plus set‑up and clean‑up.

For the youth I work with, attention spans can be short. Could we make the oral health talk more activity‑based, like a quiz or myth‑busting game, rather than a long explanation? That might also help with engagement, which is a risk in the project description.

Good point. I can rework the oral health education part in A5 into a short quiz and a demonstration with a model, instead of a long talk. That should still fit within 20 minutes. I will check with the dental clinic supervisor to ensure the messages stay aligned with clinical guidelines.

For T7 and A7, I can create simple handouts for the oral health sessions: one page with key messages and a small checklist youth can take home. I will keep the language straightforward and include visuals so it works for different literacy levels.

On feasibility for D6, if we schedule oral health sessions at the clinic youth room and community centre only, we can cluster screenings to reduce set‑up time. Doing full screenings at the school might stretch us, especially if we also run workshops there. I recommend we limit screenings to clinic and community centre for the pilot, and keep school‑based oral health to short talks only if needed.

I agree with moving the online life and safety session earlier. Proposed new sequence: 1) getting to know each other and ground rules, 2) stress, coping, and family pressures, 3) online life and safety, 4) friendships and peer pressure, 5) emotions and mood, 6) health and sleep, 7) planning for the future, 8) celebration and next steps. Unless there are strong objections, I will update A4 and T3 to reflect this for D5.
That updated sequence works well from my side. It matches what young people usually bring up in conversations, and starting with ground rules and stress feels safe.

I am comfortable limiting full oral health screenings to the clinic youth room and community centre for this pilot. At the school, I can support with short awareness inputs during workshops if time allows, but not full screenings. For D6, we can state that clearly so expectations are managed with school leadership and the dental clinic supervisor.

I will start formatting the session plans and handouts in A4 based on the new sequence and share drafts for T7. I will also prepare a simple overview sheet that shows which sessions can be combined with oral health inputs, so we can coordinate better on the day.

Once D5 and D6 are locked, I will integrate the workshop sequence and oral health sessions into the field schedule in A6 under T6. I will mark which weeks include oral health at each site so we can plan materials and travel accordingly.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on field visit schedule, logistics, and coordination with schools.

messages.text: I have posted a draft Field Visit Schedule and Location Map (A6) based on T6, using the target groups and locations agreed under D1 and the activities from A4 and A5. The proposal is: Mondays – school workshops; Wednesdays – community centre workshops; Thursdays – clinic youth room workshops and oral health; with some flexibility for exam weeks. Please review and flag any clashes or safeguarding concerns before we confirm D7.

Thanks for pulling this together. From a workshop facilitation point of view, the pattern of one main group session per site per week is workable. We just need to check with school leadership that Monday afternoons do not clash with key lessons or exams. I can reach out to the school to discuss the draft A6 and adjust if needed.

Looking at A6, I am a bit concerned about having back‑to‑back sessions on some days if we add one‑to‑one follow‑ups after workshops. I may need at least 30 minutes buffer after each group session to speak with any young person who asks for extra support. Could we build that into T6 so it is visible?

For oral health under T5 and T11, Thursdays at the clinic youth room work well, but I would prefer not to have oral health sessions immediately after a long workshop, so we have time to set up and clean up. Could we schedule oral health either at the start of the clinic slot or on alternate weeks to avoid overload?

From the documentation side, the schedule in A6 is clear enough for me to plan printing and materials under T7 and to prepare attendance sheets in A3. Once D7 is confirmed, I will create a simple calendar view for staff who prefer a visual overview.

Good point on buffer time. I can adjust T6 so that each workshop slot includes 30 minutes after the session for informal follow‑up and case notes. That will slightly reduce the number of groups we can see in a day, but it is safer and more realistic.

For oral health, I suggest we schedule them on alternate Thursdays at the clinic youth room and every second Wednesday at the community centre, with no more than two oral health groups per day. I will mark those clearly in A6 so we can plan materials and staffing under T11 and A7.

I have spoken with the deputy head at the main secondary school. They prefer Tuesdays instead of Mondays for workshops, to avoid clashes with core subjects. They are fine with a regular weekly slot for the 3‑month pilot. I propose we update A6 to move school sessions to Tuesday afternoons and keep community centre on Wednesdays and clinic on Thursdays.

I will update T6 and A6 to reflect school workshops on Tuesdays, community centre on Wednesdays, and clinic youth room on Thursdays, with built‑in buffer time and alternate‑week oral health sessions as discussed. Once updated, I will share the revised schedule for a final check before we confirm D7.

The updated pattern works for me. Having fixed days for each site will also help me plan outreach and follow‑up under T1 and T10. I will let the social services manager know the proposed days so they are aware of when we are in each location.

Alternate‑week oral health sessions on Wednesdays and Thursdays are manageable. I will use A7 to keep track of materials and make sure we have enough disposable items ready before each session, as per T11.

Once D7 is confirmed, I will prepare a one‑page schedule summary for staff and a simple note we can share with youth so they know when and where sessions happen. I will base it on the final A6 and store it with A1.

If there are no further objections, I propose we record D7 as: weekly outreach schedule locked with school workshops on Tuesdays, community centre sessions on Wednesdays, and clinic youth room sessions on Thursdays, including alternate‑week oral health sessions at community centre and clinic, with 30‑minute buffer after each workshop. I will now send A6 to school leadership and the community health coordinator for confirmation and note any minor timing tweaks, but the structure will stay as agreed.

threads.thread_goal: Review early pilot data, adjust approach, and plan evaluation outputs.

messages.text: I have compiled the first monthly summary of attendance and feedback using A3 and shared draft tables for T12. Overall, we have higher participation at the community centre than at the school, and oral health sessions at the clinic are well attended but with some no‑shows. In this thread, we should discuss any mid‑pilot adjustments and outline key points for the final evaluation in A8 for D8.

Looking at the tables, I notice that some school sessions have lower attendance, especially on weeks with tests. Young people told me they were not allowed to leave class. Maybe we need to adjust timing with the school or offer a make‑up session at the community centre for those who miss out.

That matches what I have seen. For mid‑pilot adjustment, I suggest we agree with the school to avoid workshop slots during test weeks and, where that is not possible, we run an extra open session at the community centre that week. We should also capture in A8 that school timetables are a key factor for future scale‑up.

For oral health, the data show good attendance but a few young people leave before screenings because they have to catch transport. Maybe we should move screenings earlier in the session or prioritise those who say they might need to leave early. I can also shorten the quiz slightly to free up time.

From the feedback forms in A3, youth at the community centre rate the sessions slightly higher on feeling heard and included. Comments mention the space feeling more relaxed. It might be worth reflecting in A8 that informal settings can support engagement, especially for those who do not feel comfortable at school.

We can adjust the schedule in A6 so that oral health screenings happen earlier in the clinic sessions, with the quiz and discussion afterwards. I will also flag in T12 tables how many youth started but did not complete screenings, so we can show this as a learning point in A8.

I agree about the community centre. Some young people who avoid school sessions do come there. I can step up outreach for those who miss school workshops by inviting them personally to the community centre sessions and explaining that it is the same content.

On safeguarding, the logs under T8 show a few disclosures related to family stress and online bullying. Procedures in A2 seem to be working, but we should note in A8 that staff needed time after sessions to follow up, which reinforces the importance of buffer time in the schedule.

I can start drafting sections of A8 that cover: 1) participation trends by site, 2) feedback on feeling safe and included, 3) early lessons on scheduling and safeguarding. I will base this on T10 summaries, T12 tables, and the qualitative comments from A3.

For mid‑pilot adjustments, I will propose to the school that we skip or reschedule sessions during test weeks and instead run an extra community centre session that week, as you suggested. I will track attendance before and after this change in T12 so we can see if it improves participation.

I will adjust the flow of oral health sessions so screenings happen first, then the quiz and discussion. I will also note in my records under T11 how many youth we manage to screen each time, so we can compare across sites later.

For T10, I will start adding a short weekly note in this channel summarising: attendance highlights, any safeguarding concerns (without names), and suggestions for small adjustments. That should make it easier to feed into A8 later.

For D8, I suggest we agree on three main mid‑pilot adjustments: 1) avoid school sessions during test weeks and offer extra community centre sessions instead, 2) move oral health screenings earlier in the clinic sessions, 3) strengthen outreach to youth who miss school sessions by inviting them to community centre sessions. For the final evaluation in A8, we will highlight: engagement differences by site, the importance of flexible scheduling, and the need for buffer time for follow‑up.
I will update the schedule in A6 and the data tables in T12 to reflect these adjustments, and I will add a short note in A8 explaining how the changes affected attendance and completion of sessions.

I will incorporate D8 into the draft A8 and mark clearly which findings come from mid‑pilot adjustments versus initial design. That should help stakeholders see what worked and what might need more testing if the programme is scaled up.
